name: Opposition to immigration
summary: Opposition to immigration holds that a country should sharply reduce or stop immigration, on grounds of cultural continuity, national sovereignty over borders, fiscal and labor-market burden, and security. Adherents typically want immigrants who remain to assimilate, welfare reserved for citizens, and stricter citizenship. The position cuts across the economic left and right, and its strands range from civic to ethnic nationalism.
scope: The mainstream of contemporary restrictionism as expressed by populist and national-conservative parties (Sweden Democrats, One Nation, Hungary's government) and the historical Powell speech of 1968. It excludes ethnonationalist and white-supremacist fringes (remigration, race-mixing bans), and since the ideology has no economic program, most non-immigration answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Restrictionist parties are split: Sweden Democrats back a welfare state but for citizens, while US and Australian strands are market-leaning; the ideology itself has no line on health systems.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Some restrictionists argue immigration undercuts low wages and favor wage floors, others are market-leaning; the position is not defined by the ideology.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents range from free-market conservatives to welfare-state nationalists, so the ideology is indifferent on markets in general.

public-ownership.rationale: Mostly right-of-centre parties that leave industry private, though some nationalist parties accept state ownership of utilities; inferred, not stated.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nationalist-populist parties are divided between tax-cutting and populist redistribution; the opposition to immigration is independent of this.

unions-good.rationale: Restrictionists sometimes cite worker wage protection, yet many parties are indifferent or hostile to unions; no settled stance.

property-fundamental.rationale: No documented position; adherents vary between property-rights conservatives and welfare nationalists.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Hanson attacks elites and bureaucrats but not corporate regulation as such; the ideology is split on it.

cut-welfare.rationale: The Sweden Democrats support the welfare state but limit it to citizens and residents, so the claim that welfare as such should be cut is not the ideology's, while others in the family do favor cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not a topic for restrictionist programs; inferred from their generally non-socialist orientation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security is a standard restrictionist argument for border control, and adherents generally accept strong counter-terror powers, but surveillance is not discussed directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Law-and-order and social-conservative leanings in nationalist parties make legalization unlikely, though it is not a defining issue.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Restrictionists typically complain that criticism of immigration is silenced and reject laws on hate speech as curbs on open debate; Powell similarly argued against anti-discrimination law.

strong-leader.rationale: Populist rhetoric against elites can favor decisive leaders, but many restrictionist parties operate within parliaments and defend constitutional order.

state-harmful.rationale: Restrictionism rests on the state's right to control borders and membership, so it is flatly incompatible with abolishing the state.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; restrictionists in the US and Australia lean pro-gun, though European strands are mixed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Border enforcement, deportation and crime-and-security arguments lead restrictionists to favor stronger police and border forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Social-conservative leanings suggest opposition, but it is not a defined position.

decide-locally.rationale: Some propose devolution to local communities, but restrictionists mostly want national control over borders; split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Restrictionists generally favor tough responses to crime and deportation of foreign offenders; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Social-conservative stance common among national-conservative parties, but not definitional to opposing immigration.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Adherents are split: some Western populist parties accept it or use it against Islam, while others oppose it.

abortion-legal.rationale: No shared position among restrictionist parties, which vary from pro-choice to pro-life.

more-religion-public.rationale: Some stress a Christian cultural heritage, others are secular and oppose Islam on secular grounds; split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Hanson ended with 'one people, one nation' and attacked the 'Aboriginal industry' and special group programs; Powell objected to a 'privileged or special class', so adherents reject group-targeted remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: National-conservative strands tend to reject it, though not part of the core.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural preservation is one of the central stated reasons for restricting immigration, and a shared national and cultural identity is a stated aim of the Sweden Democrats.

gradual-change.rationale: Preserving cultural continuity implies resisting rapid demographic and social change, but the point is inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Reducing immigration is the defining position: Hanson wanted it halted short term, Powell wanted inflow cut to 'negligible proportions', and Sweden Democrats seek asylum migration near zero.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Hanson called for withdrawal from the UN and the Sweden Democrats oppose shifting power to the EU, framing international bodies as threats to national control of borders.

free-trade.rationale: Adherents are divided between market-liberal restrictionists and protectionist populists; Hanson was protectionist, other parties are not.

nation-first.rationale: Restrictionism puts the national interest and the right to decide admissions ahead of cosmopolitan duties; SEP lists national interest and self-determination among its arguments.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Hanson and similar populists oppose foreign entanglements and aid; refugee-producing interventions are also disliked, but this is inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders are the direct opposite of the ideology; SEP treats restriction as the opposing pole.

limit-growth.rationale: Some restrictionists use environmental strain and population growth as an argument against immigration, but they do not generally call for limits on economic growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Mixed: some Greens-adjacent restrictionists cite sustainability, but most national-populist parties are skeptical of drastic climate policy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mainstream restrictionist parties work through elections; the rare militant strand differs.

experts-over-public.rationale: Populist restrictionists present themselves as against out-of-touch elites and bureaucrats and favor popular opinion on immigration.

central-planning.rationale: Opposed or ignored by restrictionist parties, which are not planning-oriented; inferred from their orientation.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from general non-socialist orientation.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design is outside the immigration question, and the sources show no restrictionist line on land taxation.

basic-income.rationale: Restrictionists generally prefer welfare linked to citizenship and work, which is hard to square with an unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Hanson-style populists favor protection, while market-liberal restrictionists do not; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Populist rhetoric favors small owners and farmers, but it is not a stated program.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Entirely foreign to the ideology; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Some populist parties attack central banks, others do not.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not part of the ideology; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Restrictionist parties compete in multiparty elections; Hanson attacks the big parties but wants more representation, not one-party rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Populist restrictionists commonly appeal to the will of the voters, citing majorities who want less immigration, though they dispute elite-driven outcomes.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums are used by restrictionists (for instance Hungary's 2016 quota vote), though not universal.

natural-rulers.rationale: Populists say they oppose elites, but the ideology does not generally endorse natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mainstream restrictionist parties disavow violence, but not a stated principle.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not part of the mainstream restrictionist program.

separate-church-state.rationale: Split between secular and Christian-heritage strands.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Control of borders and security is a core state function in restrictionist arguments.

military-superiority.rationale: Restrictionist parties differ on defense spending and the sources give no common line on military superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The strands split: ethnic-nationalists want a mono-ethnic nation, civic restrictionists like the Sweden Democrats say foreign-born people can become Swedish by assimilating.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rejected by nationalist framing of national unity; inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hanson and similar reject group-based programs; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Hanson called for sweeping changes to Aboriginal affairs and attacked separate Aboriginal programs.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the nation-first stance and the article's note on immigrants as colonizers claims.

civilizational-union.rationale: Some restrictionists favour defending a Western or European civilization, others stress sovereign nations; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: National self-interest is explicit but individual self-interest is not addressed.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Sweden Democrats' citizenship proposals stress loyalty and duties, but this is not a general stance.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental strain is cited against immigration, but no source shows adherents taking a view on nature's intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Some cite population growth and sprawl in the case for restriction, but they do not call for limiting native births.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a preference for continuity.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics falls outside the documented program of restrictionist parties, so no direction can be inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Distrust of elites and institutions suggests skepticism; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Security arguments suggest a lean to government access but this is not documented.

restore-past-order.rationale: Powell and others point to a feared loss of a familiar national character, but this is inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Restrictionists cite research and results when arguing their case, but also appeal to identity and principle; no consistent stance.

direct-action.rationale: Mainstream restrictionism works through parties and elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: A process-ethics claim that restrictionist sources do not take up; adherents have no shared view.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Welfare for citizens only, conditional on membership, runs against universal need-based distribution.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not stated; inferred from non-Marxist orientation.

taxation-theft.rationale: Sweden Democrats support a welfare state; some in the family differ.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Restrictionists stress national community and loyalty, but this is not a stated position on group rights.

conscription.rationale: Nationalist parties differ on national service, and Hanson called for it while others do not, so this is split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Restrictionism treats entry as a state decision and places weight on membership; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens as customers who can leave sits oddly with an emphasis on membership and borders, but no source addresses it.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not stated; inferred from conservative leanings.

media-academia-power.rationale: Restrictionists commonly claim that media and academia suppress debate on immigration, and Hanson attacked bureaucrats and 'do-gooders'.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Present in some ethnonationalist strands, rejected by civic restrictionists; the article ties opposition more to ethnocentrism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Some strands speak of national renewal, others do not.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Restrictionism focuses on closing borders, not expanding them.

universal-morality.rationale: Restrictionists dispute that universal duties require open admission, but they do not generally deny universal morals; no clear stance.

single-common-good.rationale: Appeals to one national identity point one way while parties compete as interest-based; no documented line.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Views differ: some European restrictionists are pro-Israel, others hostile.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Ethnic-nation strands favor return of co-ethnics, but this candidate is not addressed in sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language of the state matters in citizenship tests, but reviving a lapsed language is not a restrictionist concern.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding models are not part of the immigration debate and parties differ.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal burden of immigrants is argued, yet adherents split on general deficit policy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Market-liberal and welfare-nationalist strands disagree about the link between political and economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: No stated position; populist adherents emphasize law enforcement and elections over rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Political self-determination is a leading justification for controlling admission; the Sweden Democrats campaign to protect national sovereignty.

force-without-un.rationale: Hanson wanted to leave the UN, but that does not imply willingness to use force abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Some restrictionists defend Christian heritage and others a secular stance, so no common line on reason versus faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The Sweden Democrats oppose welfare for people who are not citizens or permanent residents, and welfare burden is a core restrictionist argument.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Fits a welfare-chauvinist stance, but only partly stated.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hanson blamed elites yet stressed national unity, and parties vary on the employer-worker relation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defense of inherited national culture and tradition is central, so sacrificing heritage institutions is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from nation-first outlook.

workers-nation.rationale: Restrictionists frame workers as a national group needing protection from low-wage competition, but this is partial.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social-conservative parties lean toward it, while others in the family are liberal on gender; split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Mainstream restrictionism rejects legally enforced racial separation and the Sweden Democrats say the foreign-born can become Swedish; ethnonationalist fringes dissent.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy differs across restrictionist parties and is not tied to immigration.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Hanson said immigrants must give 'full, undivided loyalty' and criticized ghettos, and the Sweden Democrats demand assimilation over integration of cultures.

elite-replacement.rationale: The Great Replacement idea is held by part of the far right, but mainstream restrictionists mostly cite elite indifference, not deliberate replacement; adherents are split.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parties benefit differently under each system.

national-mission.rationale: Nation-first restrictionists generally do not seek to spread their government abroad.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Hanson attacked 'fat cats, bureaucrats and do-gooders' and populism is tied to anti-immigration attitudes in the article.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Law-and-order support for security forces points one way and rule-of-law claims the other; no source addresses it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Border control is a core state function, but adherents differ on a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Present on the ethnonationalist fringe but not in mainstream restrictionism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mainstream adherents formally accept equal worth but reject equal claims to admission; Powell objected to special legal status, while Hanson spoke of citizens who must give loyalty.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist internal debate with no bearing on restrictionist doctrine.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The article notes that framing immigrants as colonizers comes from decolonization advocates; restrictionist nationalists reject describing their own states that way.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Hanson's one-law, one-flag stance and Sweden Democrats' common-identity stance imply the same laws for all citizens.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Restrictionists do not seek laws on conversion; a concern about Islam does not translate to restricting individual conversion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian-heritage and secular strands disagree on religious instruction in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine; restrictionists reject socialism, so they would not endorse a stronger socialist state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Restrictionists cite majority opposition and democratic legitimacy, but it is not a stated principle.

trade-surplus.rationale: Protectionist strands favor it, liberals do not.

population-transfer.rationale: Powell backed voluntary re-emigration with grants and some propose remigration, but most mainstream parties do not require departure.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state's authority to enforce borders and deport conflicts with an absolute rule.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social-Darwinist strands exist on the fringe, but mainstream restrictionism does not state this.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents often protest bans of their own parties, though not uniformly.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory of liberty that restrictionist sources do not address.

separated-powers.rationale: Support for constitutional order is typical, but populists attack judges blocking deportations; mixed.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Welfare for citizens first is an inverse of this, but poor-first language appears in the populist stance; split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing pressure is cited against immigration, but ownership rights for tenants are not a stated issue.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor law is not part of the restrictionist program, and populist parties differ on unions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Some cite population pressure abroad, but adherents generally do not stress it.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Opponents argue that immigrants form separate communities, the Sweden Democrats say a shared identity underlies cohesion, and Hanson said a multicultural country 'can never be strong or united'.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Security arguments push partly toward yes, but adherents differ.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economic intervention in scarcity is not addressed by restrictionist sources; parties differ.

party-controls-media.rationale: Restrictionists claim that existing media silence them, so they resist control of media by a ruling party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The Sweden Democrats seek strict citizenship requirements including language, cultural knowledge and loyalty, and SEP notes delayed benefits as a middle path.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Populist anti-elite appeal might support it, but not stated.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party organisation is not addressed; populist parties vary in structure.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Sweden Democrats oppose power shifting to the EU, and Hungary rejected EU migrant quotas.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional design differs across the countries where restrictionist parties operate.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the ideology's concerns.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not stated; restrictionists object to speech restrictions on themselves, but some social conservatives favor censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not part of the immigration debate, and adherents have no shared view.

recall-officials.rationale: Hanson wanted politicians who push separatism to lose their seats, but recall is not discussed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Hanson-style isolationism favors it, but other parties support alliances like NATO; split.

people-in-arms.rationale: Gun-rights supporters among restrictionists might like it, but the sources contain no stated position.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural populist appeal exists but is not stated as a moral claim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Education is the strongest predictor of opposition in the article, and populist adherents attack 'do-gooders' and elites as out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Opposition to multiculturalism rests on the claim that cultures differ in ways that matter; Sweden Democrats favor assimilation into one culture. Some adherents would still call cultures merely different.

death-penalty.rationale: Law-and-order populists lean toward it, but not stated.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Social conservatives within the family oppose it, but no stated position.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Restrictionists tend to prefer descent or strict requirements over birthright citizenship, and the Sweden Democrats ask citizenship be earned through assimilation.

minority-language-support.rationale: Hanson wanted one people, and assimilation is demanded; support for minority-language provision runs counter.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Opposition to separate customs and parallel communities makes exemptions from general laws unwelcome.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Expectation that immigrants conform implies conformity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Hanson opposed foreign aid, so debt cancellation is likely rejected.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A postcolonial economic argument outside restrictionist concerns; no stated position.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Restrictionists work within existing constitutions, and rewriting procedure is not addressed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Not stated; inferred from electoral stance.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The article notes some restrictionists favor aid in origin countries instead of admitting migrants, but Hanson opposed foreign aid; a duty to give substantial aid is not accepted.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Defense posture differs between restrictionist parties and is not tied to immigration.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Populist favor for popular votes suggests a lean, but there is no stated position.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Populists attack central banks in some places and accept them in others; split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims are outside the ideology, and nationalist leanings are not a stated rule.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Market-liberal and welfare-nationalist strands differ on the limits of property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A left-wing debate about Soviet history that restrictionists have no position on.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Security arguments invoke caution about risk, but environmental precaution is not a stated stance.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International-law questions on annexation are not addressed by restrictionist sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Strands differ: secular ones want religion subordinate to the state in relation to Islam, while Christian-heritage ones do not.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional preferences vary by country, and nothing is stated.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: National unity favors it, but no source addresses it and adherents differ by case.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; national-unity instincts point against it, but regional autonomy is also a populist theme.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not a restrictionist issue, and market-liberal and welfare-nationalist strands differ.

character-from-environment.rationale: Environmental and innate views are both found.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not part of the ideology; parties compete under constitutions.

space-expansion.rationale: No restrictionist source addresses space policy.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional theory is not addressed by restrictionist sources.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunifying a divided nation is not addressed by restrictionist sources, though nationalist sympathies might incline toward it.

leader-cult.rationale: Not addressed; restrictionist parties operate within liberal-democratic politics and frame themselves as anti-elite, so public glorification of a leader is not part of the position, though some parties are leader-centred.

equal-parenting.rationale: The ideology has no line on custody law; the position cuts across the economic and social left and right, so nothing can be inferred beyond indifference.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: restrictionism is not a class-based doctrine and its mainstream parties accept the existing political order.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: restrictionist parties mostly defend property and have no land-reform program.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred: adherents want returns of those with no claim to stay, but not an open-ended right of return for descendants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: mainstream restrictionism focuses on controlling its own borders, though some governments back kin-state claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: restrictionists oppose penalising belief and often cite freedom of religion and conscience against Islamic law.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred: restrictionist parties have backed burqa bans, and they oppose imposed religious dress codes.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty stance: the Sweden Democrats oppose euro adoption and EU integration.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: the focus is on the nation-state and its borders, not on political union of kindred peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Restrictionists demand assimilation and an end to multiculturalism rather than separate minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The ideology is about the receiving country and has no stated line on where persecuted minorities should settle.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: restrictionists stress culture and national identity as drivers of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not addressed and adherents range from market-liberal to economic-nationalist.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; populist restrictionists are split between market-leaning and protectionist views.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: populist restrictionists often attack courts and international bodies that block migration policy chosen by voters.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: restrictionist parties are mostly conservative on gender and oppose quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Split: economic-nationalist strands favour protection but market-liberal strands favour trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between market-leaning and protectionist views.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: no restrictionist text calls for moral incentives, and mainstream strands accept pay incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred: mainstream restrictionism works through elections and law and rejects armed revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Split: Powell was a monarchist conservative while other strands, like Hanson, say nothing about titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cultural continuity and assimilation are core restrictionist aims, so a nation-centred curriculum is inferred as the preferred approach.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Restrictionism stresses national sovereignty and self-determination and has no program of ruling other peoples; inferred from its anti-UN, sovereigntist stance.

patriotic-education.rationale: Assimilation into a shared national culture is a standard demand, so schools teaching national loyalty is inferred as consistent.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Restrictionists such as Hanson and Powell opposed group-specific treatment and race relations law; inferred, as the ideology has no admissions policy.

public-money-creation.rationale: The ideology has no monetary program and adherents range from market-leaning to populist.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Nothing in the ideology bears on capitalism's stability; adherents span left and right economics.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Powell and later restrictionists reject special ties with former imperial territories and Commonwealth migration; inferred from that stance.

delink-world-market.rationale: Populist restrictionists such as Hanson often oppose globalisation and free trade, though the ideology is not defined by it; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Restrictionists argue citizen workers are harmed by immigration competition, a framing at odds with the claim that rich-country workers are not exploited; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Powell opposed race-relations law, but civic-nationalist strands accept anti-discrimination law; adherents are split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The ideology has no stance on entrenched rights; some strands cite constitutional limits, others favour parliamentary or popular sovereignty.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: No documented position; the ideology concerns immigration, not colonial borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: No documented position on monarchy or succession.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: restrictionists favor majoritarian democracy, with referendums on immigration, over minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: No documented position on resistance to rulers; populist strands appeal to people against elites but that is not defined by the ideology.

parliament-supreme.rationale: No documented position on lawmaking authority.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology has no stance on animals and strands differ.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: mainstream restrictionist parties accept humane animal use; the Sweden Democrats' program includes animal-welfare planks.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Not defined by the ideology; welfare-chauvinist strands support the needy at home but others oppose redistribution.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Restrictionist movements are politically engaged and mobilize voters, but withdrawal is not addressed directly. Inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; strands of populism accuse the media of elite bias, but no pacification thesis.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: No documented position on the hegemony thesis.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: nationalist restrictionists do not typically adopt dependency theory, and Hanson attacked international bodies as globalist.

native-born-offices.rationale: Welfare-for-citizens and stricter-citizenship positions suggest preferring citizens, but reserving offices for native-born is more extreme than most restrictionists hold; mild lean toward agree.

party-own-road.rationale: Not applicable; not a communist or socialist current.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Hanson and the Sweden Democrats favor national self-reliance and oppose foreign influence; inferred for aid and investment, with moderate confidence.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The ideology concerns migration not territory; Hungary's government has made some such claims, but the strand is split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: restrictionists stress the existing nation and its culture, and the statement is about indigenous leadership over settler descendants, which most reject.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: restrictionist parties are mostly on the right and doubt this framing, though the question is not defining.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Many national-conservative restrictionists condemn both communism and fascism; inferred and split across strands.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: No documented position on the Civil War.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: national-conservative restrictionists generally oppose removing national monuments and symbols.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Hanson and national-conservative strands reject universalism and defend distinct national cultures; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: mainstream restrictionist parties stay within civilian democratic politics.

paid-care-work.rationale: No documented position; strands are split.

filial-duty.rationale: National-conservative restrictionists stress family and cultural continuity, but the ideology has no stated line on filial duty; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Restrictionism has no position on how officials are chosen; inferred as indifference.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Restrictionist parties stress national sovereignty and often object to foreign ownership of national assets; inferred from that principle.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Restrictionists are split between socially conservative and liberal strands on divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Populists favour direct democracy in places, but the ideology has no position on binding delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Restrictionists are split between market-leaning and welfare-state strands on pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Restrictionist parties generally defend private property and citizen ownership rather than communal land with use-based tenure; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parties stressing national sovereignty typically defend parliamentary control of spending; inferred, with no direct source.

single-official-language.rationale: Assimilation is a core restrictionist demand, and a common national language is its usual first requirement.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Hanson and similar platforms want national assets and land kept in citizen hands; inferred from sovereignty arguments.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Powell and later restrictionists opposed race-relations law and anti-discrimination measures, so outcome-based tests are inferred to be rejected.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Restrictionism has no position on consumerism; the ideology is about borders.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Restrictionist parties tend toward non-intervention and sovereignty, so arming foreign insurgents is inferred to be disfavoured.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Defence of national sovereignty is inferred to extend to opposing great-power intervention in allied states.

corporate-influence.rationale: Populist restrictionists often blame business elites for favouring cheap immigrant labour, though the ideology has no line on lobbying; inferred from that populist framing.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Hungary's government, a model for this strand, restricts foreign-funded NGOs on sovereignty grounds; inferred from the sovereignty argument for border control.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Restrictionists who want fewer immigrants usually prefer family incentives to immigration as the answer to population decline; inferred, not a stated demand in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: The ideology is about who enters the country, not who may buy property, and adherents are split on local purchase limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment policy is outside the ideology and its parties split between market-leaning and welfare-state positions.

democratic-peace.rationale: The ideology takes no line on democracy promotion; adherents are often sceptical of foreign adventures but others back a democratic West.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Restrictionists stress law enforcement and rule of law at the border, so they reject a general freedom to disregard law; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Restrictionists tend to favour staying out of foreign conflicts but many back intervention against security threats, so no common line.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is unrelated to the ideology and adherents span left and right economic positions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The mainstream strand in scope rejects the Great Replacement-style conspiracy claims that belong to the ethnonationalist fringe the profile excludes.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Adherents lean to traditional family and national-continuity concerns, so they favour keeping legal marriage; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Adherents are split: populists attack secretive elites, while national-security arguments favour confidentiality.

local-production.rationale: Protectionist and nationalist strands favour buying local and national production; inferred from economic nationalism.

informal-organisation.rationale: These adherents mostly organise through parties such as the Sweden Democrats and One Nation, not informal affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Control of borders is argued as a sovereign right, so adherents want national law to prevail over international courts and refugee rules.

religious-nation.rationale: Strands range from civic to ethnic nationalism, and the Sweden Democrats and One Nation define belonging by culture more than faith, while Hungary's government stresses Christian identity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Restrictionist parties stress national sovereignty and independence, so ritual submission to a leading power runs against the stance; inferred from that sovereignty emphasis.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The ideology has no regional fiscal line and adherents are split, so this is left neutral.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The ideology is silent on property and its parties span market and welfare positions.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism is not part of the stance itself, and some adherents hold it while others do not.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Restrictionist parties are split between welfare-state and market-leaning positions, with no line on who delivers services.

religion-illusion.rationale: The stance concerns immigration, and adherents are split between religious defenders of cultural heritage and secular ones.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: No stated view on capitalism's historical role; strands range from market-leaning to welfare-nationalist.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: National-conservative restrictionists generally seek reform within existing institutions rather than economic transformation; inferred from their programmes.

socialized-care.rationale: Restrictionist parties such as the Sweden Democrats favour traditional family arrangements and do not call for socialised housework; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Assimilation is a common demand, but a campaign against loanwords is not a documented part of the stance.

treaties-binding.rationale: The ideology has no line on treaties with internal nations; adherents are split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Restrictionists defend the existing nation-state and its institutions, so a reorganisation into communes is unlikely; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Assimilation of minorities is favoured, but state-directed settlement into minority regions is not a documented position of the mainstream.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The ideology has no economic programme and strands accept either capitalism or welfare arrangements.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Restrictionists stress a nation's ancestral ties and cultural continuity, though the civic strand rests on citizenship rather than descent.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The mainstream restrictionist parties disavow Holocaust denial, and the scope excludes ethnonationalist fringes.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Mainstream restrictionist parties in Western countries do not campaign to criminalise homosexuality; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Restrictionist parties compete in elections and complain of being shut out, so they oppose suppression of opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: mainstream restrictionists defend free speech, though some favour protecting Christian heritage.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: the movement is inward-looking and nation-centred, not a colonial project.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is an Islamic religious obligation that restrictionists regard as a security concern, not one they hold.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: it opposes political Islam and religious takeover of government.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Populist parties favour referendums and distrust distant officials, though they do not stress workplace or university participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: restrictionist politics generally rejects identity-politics frameworks.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the national-conservative stance of the main restrictionist parties; not part of the immigration question.

assisted-dying.rationale: Adherents are split and the ideology has no position.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Restrictionist populists often claim to be beyond left and right, as the Sweden Democrats do with welfare-plus-nationalism.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: Marxist concept; restrictionist economic arguments centre on wages and labour supply, not alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Mainstream restrictionist speakers and parties commonly argue Islam clashes with national culture, though civic strands dispute this.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: the movement rests on national sovereignty and the people, not divine authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: restrictionists tend to support limits on Islamic dress in state institutions, though Christian conservatives among them dissent.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The ideology is not concerned with employment contracts or workplace harassment, so no position is documented; inferred as neutral.

social-market-economy.rationale: Many restrictionist parties favour welfare reserved for citizens within a market economy; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement stresses border security and sovereignty, which presuppose armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: nationalist-populists tend to stress equal treatment of citizens over staged inequality.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Adherents differ, from Atlanticist to sovereigntist; no common position.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Restrictionist parties are mostly republican or electoral nationalists and the ideology has no line on succession; most adherents would reject hereditary succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Restrictionism has no economic programme; adherents are split on mutual banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Populist restrictionists such as One Nation and the Sweden Democrats stress national sovereignty against international bodies, so they tend to resist IMF conditions; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Restrictionist parties are electoral and populist and defend universal suffrage for citizens; a property bar is not part of the platform.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The ideology does not address ecofeminist theory, and its conservative and nationalist strands would reject the claim.

reification.rationale: This is a Marxist claim and restrictionists, mostly on the nationalist right, do not hold it; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Populist restrictionists often attack media elites as hostile, but they do not generally attack property in presses; adherents are split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Restrictionists are usually conservative and rule-of-law minded, though populists attack unelected judges; the majority would accept the claim, inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The scope excludes ethnonationalist fringes; mainstream restrictionists such as the Sweden Democrats and One Nation back equal citizenship for those who become citizens.

online-participation.rationale: The ideology has no line on online participation; populist parties often favour referendums but adherents are split on internet deliberation.

open-government-data.rationale: Anti-elite populists may favour transparency, but the ideology has no stated line on open records; adherents are split.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The mainstream scope rejects race and religion tests for the vote, but some adherents back cultural criteria for entry; most would not support marriage law restrictions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The mainstream scope excludes bigoted fringes, and restrictionist parties seek assimilation, not boycotts of minority shops.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Populist restrictionists favour referendums and distrust elites, but have no stated line on lot-chosen assemblies, so this is inferred as split.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Restrictionists often defend inherited Christian heritage yet urge Islam to reform; the ideology has no line on doctrine, so this is inferred as split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Restrictionist parties are split between market-leaning and welfare-protecting economics, and the ideology has no economic line.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The ideology has no line on this; adherents are split between socially conservative and liberal-nationalist strands (some Western parties are gay-friendly).

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Restrictionists emphasise preserving national cultural and religious heritage, and the position is hostile to state secularist imposition; the Sweden Democrats and Hungary's government defend Christian heritage.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Security and law and order, including deporting criminal immigrants, are core arguments for restriction, so abolition is firmly opposed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: restrictionists want one national community that assimilates, and oppose group-based power-sharing, though the topic is not addressed directly.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Adherents are split: welfare-state nationalists want benefits reserved for citizens, while market-leaning strands favour private help.

term-limits.rationale: The ideology takes no position on terms in office and adherents across populist parties are split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: populist restrictionists favour direct referendums, but liquid delegation is not part of the programme and is unlikely to be supported.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: the ideology focuses on national borders, culture and security rather than global catastrophic risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The ideology has no line, and adherents range from conservative Christians to secular nationalists.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: most contemporary restrictionist parties operate in societies with legal marital equality and do not campaign for male headship, though traditionalist strands dissent.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Restrictionists reserve welfare and citizenship for citizens, so extending the franchise to non-citizens runs against their line; inferred from the stricter-citizenship stance.

rent-control.rationale: The ideology has no housing policy and restrictionist parties split between market-leaning and welfare-protective positions.

abolish-ip.rationale: No restrictionist source addresses intellectual property; the market-leaning and nationalist-conservative strands generally defend it, so this is inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not an immigration issue; national-conservative parties are mixed on youth drilling and few advocate it, inferred from their mainstream civic character.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The ideology says nothing on nuclear basing; sovereignty arguments and security arguments pull in different directions.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Border sovereignty suggests wariness of foreign control, but restrictionist parties often back alliances such as NATO, so adherents are split.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Restrictionism has no settled line on genocide recognition; individual parties differ by their own national history.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The ideology has no economic programme and its adherents range from market-liberal to welfare-chauvinist.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Mainstream restrictionists support policing and national defence and nothing in their sources suggests pacifism; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Cultural continuity is a stated ground for restriction, which implies a nation with a lasting identity, though the claim of ancient unbroken origins is stronger than most civic restrictionists make.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; national-conservative adherents typically treat sex as biological, inferred from their conservatism.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the national-conservative stance, which tends to reject identity-based feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Adherents differ; some national-conservative movements honour fallen soldiers while civic strands do not use saint language.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Mainstream restrictionism argues on security, fiscal and cultural grounds, not on a cosmic good-versus-evil view of politics; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; diaspora relations vary by country.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural continuity is central to the case, but the ideology has no stand on the order of cultural and state projects.

god-not-male.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to theological language for God, and its adherents split between religious conservatives and secular voters.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the national-conservative stance, which generally resists subjecting religious tradition to feminist tests.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The mainstream scope excludes ethnonationalist fringes; civic restrictionists want assimilation of immigrants, not control of the economy by ethnic groups, while others lean the other way.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; a mainstream restrictionist defends existing state borders and would not merge regions by ethnic group.

independent-unions.rationale: The ideology has no labour programme; restrictionist parties are split on unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The ideology does not address what counts as socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from welfare chauvinism in parties such as the Sweden Democrats, who defend public services for citizens.

second-chamber.rationale: The ideology does not address legislative structure.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: restrictionist parties are mostly market-leaning or national-state oriented, not municipal-ownership advocates.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national sovereignty and control, which disfavours pooling power in joint bodies.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from pro-family, pro-native-worker positions of national-conservative parties; not central to the ideology.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The ideology does not address drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The ideology does not address ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the security emphasis of restrictionists, which favours state ability to trace funds.

online-anonymity.rationale: The ideology does not address online identity.

person-over-state.rationale: Restrictionists emphasize the national community but do not usually deny individual worth; adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from cultural-continuity arguments and the frequent appeal to Christian or traditional heritage in national-conservative parties.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national sovereignty and a unitary nation under national control.

gm-crops.rationale: The ideology does not address agriculture.

dense-cities.rationale: Adherents are split; some blame dense, immigrant-heavy cities, others do not address the question.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The mainstream strand covered by the scope rests on civic or cultural arguments and rejects racial organizing, which belongs to excluded fringes.

racial-pride.rationale: Mainstream restrictionists speak of cultural, not racial, identity, so racial pride is not an issue they take up.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist and sovereigntist emphasis of restrictionist parties, who often oppose foreign interventions.

missingStatements.text: A country should be able to deport immigrants who commit serious crimes.
missingStatements.rationale: Deportation and returns are central restrictionist policy alongside border enforcement, and are cited in the article's policy list.

missingStatements.text: Asylum seekers should be turned back or processed outside the country rather than admitted to claim asylum on its territory.
missingStatements.rationale: The Sweden Democrats seek asylum migration near zero and the article lists deterrence and returns as policy.

missingStatements.text: Immigration costs the receiving country more in public spending than immigrants contribute.
missingStatements.rationale: The fiscal-burden claim is a main economic argument, while research cited in the article is contested.
missingStatements.declined: Fiscal-cost claim is an empirical, contested one that reduce-immigration and welfare-for-citizens already place; not worth a bank slot.

missingStatements.text: Governments should be able to decide whom to admit as a matter of national self-determination.
missingStatements.rationale: SEP treats political self-determination as a leading argument for restriction, and restrictionist parties frame admission as a sovereign choice.

notes: Strands differ: civic-assimilationist (Sweden Democrats), economic-protectionist (Hanson on unemployment), and ethnonationalist (replacement theory, remigration). Non-immigration answers vary by country; most are therefore low confidence.
